notes: China was ruled by the Ming (1368), not the Mongol Great Khanate.
The Mongols had withdrawn to the steppe as the Northern Yuan.
The Mongol khanates were independent of each other by 1400.
Added Muscovy and its neighbours Tver and Ryazan.
Japan was under the Ashikaga shogunate (1336).
Srivijaya had been absorbed by Majapahit.
The Sultanate of Rum ended in 1308; Anatolia was split among beyliks.
The White and Blue Hordes were the two wings of the Golden Horde, reunited under Tokhtamysh and Edigu.
After Timur's sack of Delhi (1398) the Sultanate held little beyond Delhi; regional sultanates and Vijayanagara ruled the rest.
Greenland: only the Norse settlements (c. 985–1450) are shown, not the whole ice sheet.
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Korea was ruled by Joseon from 1392; it no longer shows as part of the Northern Yuan.
The Blemmyes disappear from the record by the 7th century; their land is the Beja.
Teotihuacan (abandoned about 550), Monte Albán (about 850) and Classic Veracruz are replaced by the peoples of this date.
North Africa is named for its rulers of the time.
The Nile and the Horn of Africa are named for their peoples and states of the time.
Peoples who formed in the colonial era are replaced by the peoples who lived there before 1500.
Mesoamerica is named for its peoples and states of the time.
Andean and Amazonian peoples are named for their time.
North American cultures are named for their time; the Mississippi and Ohio valleys were the land of the Mississippian and Fort Ancient cultures (boxes approximate).
South-western peoples are drawn where they lived: the Mogollon and Hohokam in New Mexico and Arizona, not northern Mexico (lines approximate).
Early South American cultures are drawn where they lived (lines approximate).
Two different states with one name are named apart (for example the Kingdom of Kongo and the modern Congo).
